+18%: 35.1 Mkm² against 29.9 (±4.5 allowed). The field it is built from is the miss, not the pack law: the reanalysis' April runs 3–7°C colder than the 1991–2020 station normals across the continental interior at 55–65°N (raw 1.9° cells: Yakutsk −7.6 vs ~−4, Tomsk −1.4 vs ~2.1, Moscow 3.4 vs ~6.6, Fairbanks −6.4 vs ~0.4, Winnipeg 0.8 vs ~4.4) and 2–3.5× wetter over the boreal interior (Fairbanks 971 vs ~275 mm a year, Norilsk 981 vs ~500, Anadyr 762 vs ~350, Verkhoyansk 384 vs ~180), so the pack the field builds is deeper and its April colder than the ground the charts see — the land below 0°C in the field's April mean is 31.5 Mkm², more than the charts' whole April extent. The model's own convention (fractional cover against the charts' half-cell binary rule) accounts for at most exp(−σ²/2) ≈ 7% of the melt season's area-time, inside the band. Weekly stepping within the month took the row from +22% to +18% (dev) and +21% to +17% (target); the band was set before the first measurement and is not widened.

+24%: 22.6 Mkm² against 18.2 (±3.0 allowed). The same input as nh-extent-04: the interior's April cold bias and the boreal wet bias carry a deeper pack into a colder spring, so the field melts out two to three weeks late where the charts go bare. Weekly stepping within the month took the row from +32% to +24% (dev) and +31% to +23% (target); June is inside the band at both grids. Not tuned; the band stands.

−18%: 15.5 Mkm² against 19.0 (±3.0 allowed); the dev row passes on the absolute floor (16.0, 2.96 short). Read at a 1 mm bar the same month is 22.2 Mkm²: the pack is there but thin at the month's end across the 50–60°N belt, and a cell counts for the share of the month its pack stands above the 5 mm bar. It is not a warm bias — the field's October runs 1–3°C COLD of the stations there (Yakutsk −9.5 vs ~−7.5, Yellowknife −4.1 vs ~−1) — but the season's onset: the first snow lies at the bar for most of the month in the model, while the charts count a cell from its first white week. Weekly stepping within the month took the row from −29% to −16% (dev) and −31% to −18% (target). The bar and the band were set before the measurement; the onset (a fresh-snow depth of its own, the charts' half-cell rule) is the open mechanism, §8 of the W27 handoff.
